name: Ginsberg NDO
aliases: Phase 3 OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urinary Incontinence from Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity
question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA reduce urinary incontinence in neurogenic detrusor overactivity, and does 300 U add benefit over 200 U?

design.population: 416 adults with urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity (multiple sclerosis 227, spinal cord injury 189) and 14 or more incontinence episodes per week.
design.description: International, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Both doses beat placebo; 300 U gave no clinically relevant gain and catheterization for retention rose with dose.
takeaway: In patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity from multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and 300 U cut weekly incontinence episodes at week 6 by 21 and 23 versus 9 with placebo; catheterization for retention rose with dose.

reports.label: Phase 3 trial, 52 weeks
reports.citation: Ginsberg D, Gousse A, Keppenne V, et al. "Phase 3 Efficacy and Tolerability Study of OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urinary Incontinence From Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity." *J Urol.* 2012;187(6):2131-2139. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.01.125
reports.followUp: Primary endpoint at week 6 within a 52-week trial

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6; each dose versus placebo
results.note: P<0.001 for each dose versus placebo.

results.measure: Change in maximum cystometric capacity; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Change in maximum detrusor pressure during the first involuntary detrusor contraction; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Change in Incontinence Quality of Life total score; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Median time to patient request for re-treatment

harms.label: Clean intermittent catheterization started for urinary retention, patients not catheterizing at baseline
Most common adverse events
harms.note: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention.

delivery.label: Treatment
delivery.value: Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or 300 U, or placebo.

delivery.label: Entry criterion
delivery.value: 14 or more urinary incontinence episodes per week.

delivery.label: Dose comparison
delivery.value: No clinically relevant benefit in efficacy or duration of the 300 U dose over 200 U.

reports.label: Pooled extension interim analysis, five cycles
reports.citation: Kennelly M, Dmochowski R, Ethans K, et al. "Long-term Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Patients With Urinary Incontinence Due to Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity: An Interim Analysis." *Urology.* 2013;81(3):491-497. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2012.11.010
reports.followUp: Week 6 after each of treatment cycles 1-5
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; Results

results.measure: Change from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6 after each treatment, 200 U group, cycles 1-5

values.u200: 22.7, 23.3, 23.1, 25.3 and 31.9 fewer episodes per week, respectively

results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; Results

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in incontinence episodes
results.measure: Proportion with at least 50% reduction from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6 across cycles 1-5
results.note: 73%-94% across cycles; per-cycle responder denominators not given in abstract.

results.measure: Proportion with 100% reduction from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6 across cycles 1-5
results.note: 36%-55% across cycles; per-cycle responder denominators not given in abstract.

results.endpoint: Volume per void and quality of life
results.measure: Change in mean volume per void and Incontinence Quality of Life responses after repeat treatment
results.note: Mean volume per void increased by more than 130 mL; quality of life improved.

harms.label: Most common adverse events over repeated treatment
harms.note: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention; adverse-event profile did not change over time. Event counts and denominators not given in abstract.

delivery.label: Treatment-cycle counts
delivery.value: 387, 336, 241, 113 and 46 patients received cycles 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, respectively, pooling the preceding phase 3 studies and ongoing extension.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; Results

reports.label: Extension, up to four years
reports.citation: Kennelly M, Dmochowski R, Schulte-Baukloh H, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA Therapy Are Sustained Over 4 Years of Treatment in Patients With Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity: Final Results of a Long-Term Extension Study." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2017;36(2):368-375. doi:10.1002/nau.22934
reports.followUp: Mean 3.6 years among 388 toxin-treated patients; results shown through six treatments

results.measure: Change from study baseline in incontinence episodes per day at week 6 after each of up to six sequential treatments, among pooled phase 3/extension patients who received 200 U in that cycle (including patients previously given 300 U)
results.note: Mean reductions of 3.2 to 4.1 episodes/day (75% to 84%) across six 200-U cycles; 300-U outcomes were similar. No formal hypothesis test was planned.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 369-370

results.measure: Median time to patient request for retreatment across completed cycles, patients receiving 200 U only
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 369, 371
results.note: Among 200-U-only patients, 22% had an effect under 6 months, 52% for 6 to under 12 months and 26% for at least 12 months.

results.measure: Change in volume per void at week 6 after each treatment, 200-U cycles
results.note: Consistently increased, nearly doubling after treatment.

results.measure: Change in I-QOL total score at week 6 after each of six 200-U treatments
results.note: The minimally important difference was 11 points; 71% to 81% achieved an increase of at least 11 points across cycles.

results.measure: At least 50% and 100% reduction in daily incontinence episodes at week 6 across six 200-U treatments

values.u200: over 83% achieved at least 50% reduction; 43% to 56% achieved 100% reduction

harms.label: De novo clean intermittent catheterization among patients who had never initiated catheterization before each cycle, treatments 1 to 3 in the pooled phase 3/extension cohort
harms.note: Denominator: patients receiving that cycle who had never initiated CIC before it; no new CIC in cycles 4-6.

harms.label: Most common adverse events
harms.note: Events were assessed within 12 weeks of treatment; UTI definition included asymptomatic bacteriuria, and retention was investigator-defined. No new safety signals were identified.
harms.locator: Full text, Methods, p 369; Table II, p 373

harms.label: Toxin-neutralizing antibody seroconversion
harms.value: 8/381 (2.1%) overall; 3/200 (1.5%) among patients receiving the approved 200-U dose
harms.note: All eight had spinal cord injury; four retained at least a 50% incontinence reduction after seroconversion.

delivery.label: Extension design
delivery.value: Of 691 phase 3 enrollees, 559 completed a parent trial and 396 entered this 3-year, open-label extension; 388 received toxin and formed the efficacy/safety population. Initial 200-U or 300-U dosing continued until a 2011 amendment made all later doses 200 U; each dose used 30 cystoscopic 1-mL detrusor injections sparing the trigone. Retreatment required patient request, at least 12 weeks since the prior injection and at least one incontinence episode within 3 days.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 369-370; Results, p 370

delivery.label: Follow-up and attrition
delivery.value: 240/396 (60.6%) extension entrants were followed for at least 4 years; 8/396 (2.0%) stopped for lack of efficacy and 12/396 (3.0%) for adverse events. Mean follow-up of the 388 toxin-treated patients was 3.6 years.

reports.label: Four-year completers
reports.citation: Rovner E, Kohan A, Chartier-Kastler E, et al. "Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Patients With Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity Who Completed 4 Years of Treatment." *J Urol.* 2016;196(3):801-808. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2016.04.046
reports.followUp: 4 years; post hoc analysis of 227/388 toxin-treated completers (58.5%)

results.measure: Mean per-patient week-6 change in daily incontinence episodes across treatments within each year, among 227 four-year completers
results.note: Pooled reductions were 3.5, 3.5, 3.8 and 3.8 episodes/day in years 1-4 from a pooled baseline of 4.3/day; post hoc descriptive analysis without a hypothesis test.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 802-803; Results, p 804, Fig 3

results.measure: Reduction in incontinence episodes of at least 50% and of 100%, by treatment year
results.note: In the cohort of 227 four-year completers, rates among patients treated in each respective year at week 6 were 87.6%, 88.2%, 90.5% and 92.1% for at least 50% reduction in incontinence episodes and 46.3%, 51.7%, 53.2% and 52.0% for 100% reduction in years 1-4.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 804, Fig 4, p 805

results.note: Duration was time from injection to patient request for retreatment; the two cohorts were 200 U only and 300 U followed by 200 U.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 803; Results, p 804, Fig 2

results.note: Mean 1.5, 1.4, 1.5 and 1.5 treatments in years 1-4 among 227 completers.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in I-QOL total score at week 6 after treatment in each of four years, 227 completers
results.note: Pooled mean increases were 31.7, 30.8, 32.2 and 31.4 points in years 1-4, above the 11-point minimally important difference.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 804, Fig 5, p 806

harms.label: Most common adverse event
harms.note: Pooled 227 completers; events within 12 weeks of each injection, with treatments as denominators. Symptomatic and asymptomatic UTI were not distinguished. No new safety signals emerged over time.
harms.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 802-803; Table 2, p 806
harms.value: UTI per treatment: 73/340 (21.5%) in year 1, 54/258 (20.9%) in year 2, 42/243 (17.3%) in year 3 and 43/228 (18.9%) in year 4

harms.label: Urinary retention per treatment
harms.note: Retention was investigator-defined and assessed within 12 weeks of each treatment.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 804; Table 2, p 806

harms.label: De novo CIC among patients who had not previously catheterized, by year
harms.note: Pooled 227 completers; denominator was prior nonusers at the start of each year, and CIC initiation was investigator-defined.
harms.locator: Full text, Methods and Table 1, p 803

delivery.label: Population
delivery.value: Post hoc analysis of 227/388 (58.5%) toxin-treated four-year completers pooled from two phase 3 trials and their 3-year open-label extension: 122 received 200 U only and 105 received at least one 300 U dose; after the protocol amendment, any subsequent doses were 200 U. Retreatment required a patient request, at least 12 weeks since prior injection and at least one incontinence episode within 3 days.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Table 1, pp 802-803

relations.note: Same toxin and route tested in idiopathic OAB at 100 U; this trial used 200 U and 300 U in neurogenic detrusor overactivity.
